title: Post Oak: Ancient Post Oaks You Can Visit
meta_description: A slow, hard-wooded oak of the old Texas savanna. Downtown Dallas keeps a protected grove of them among the graves of its founding families.
intro: The post oak is a slow-growing oak with hard, dense wood, which is why it so often turns out to be the oldest thing left on ground that has been farmed, grazed and built over. Downtown Dallas keeps a whole grove of them in Pioneer Park Cemetery, among the last of the Post Oak Savanna left in any city, over the graves of its founding families. By one local reckoning the oldest are around 250 years, and in 2023 the City Council protected the stand as one of Dallas's first Historic Tree designations. The county's biggest single post oak grows in a one-acre pioneer cemetery on Military Parkway, 4.22 metres round and undated. In Fort Worth, one behind a stop sign has been spared by road crews on numerous occasions; the city's register calls it likely one of the oldest trees in Fort Worth, and gives no figure.
